title: Ambiguity: Java the language and Java the island
description: Mei complains about learning the Java programming language for a course, then Arjun says "speaking of Java" and talks about his cousin's trip to the island of Java in Indonesia. Expect two different threads and no revisit edge between them.

utterances.text: I have to learn Java for my data structures course and I hate it so much.
Oh no. Why Java? I thought everyone teaches Python now.
The prof says Java makes you think about types. Which, sure, but I spend half my time writing boilerplate.
Public static void main string args. I still have it memorised from high school.
Exactly! And the error messages are like a novel. A null pointer exception and forty lines of stack trace.
Do you have IntelliJ at least? It writes half the boilerplate for you.
Yeah, the student licence is free. It helps. I just miss how short Python is.
Ha, speaking of Java, my cousin just got back from Java, the island. She was in Indonesia for three weeks.
Oh nice! Where did she go?
Yogyakarta mostly. She did the sunrise at Borobudur, the huge Buddhist temple.
I've seen photos of that! With the mist and the volcano behind it?
Yes, that's Merapi. And then she hiked Mount Bromo at like three in the morning to see the crater.
That sounds incredible. Was it expensive?
Super cheap apparently, except the flights. She said the street food was the best part, the gudeg especially.
Okay, I'm adding Indonesia to my list. After I survive this course.
